model: TEC2647Z-3 / TEC2647Z-3+PIR Zone Controller (TEC Zoning System, BACnet MS/TP)
equipment_type: VAV zone controller (room thermostat for TEC zoning)
applies_to: Zone dampers in the Johnson Controls TEC zoning system, each run by a TEC2647Z-3 zone controller (optionally with PIR occupancy sensor) and served by a TEC2664Z-3 rooftop controller.
summary: The TEC2647Z-3 is the zone controller of the Johnson Controls TEC zoning system for constant volume, pressure-dependent rooftop units. It modulates the zone damper, can drive analog or on/off reheat, and sends weighted heating and cooling demand to its rooftop controller over BACnet MS/TP. A supervisory controller can monitor it, schedule each zone, or take full control, depending on Cfg Network Handle.
notes: Objects from Table 23 of the TEC zoning technical bulletin (LIT-12011682), pages 61-64; the device object (TEC2647Z-72aaa) is not listed as a point.

Access follows the table footnotes. GUI Room Temperature (AV 21) is writable only while GUI Room Temp Override (BV 10) = Override; GUI Occupancy (MV 9) only when Cfg Network Handle is 2 or 3; Sta RTC Smart Recovery (BV 11) and Sta RTC Zone Sequencing (MV 10) only when it is 3.

The -2 edition of the bulletin (TEC2647Z-2) lists the same objects except GUI P1 Heat/Cool Demand (AV 24/25) and Cfg Setpoint Type (BV 12); its GUI Occupancy states are Released, Occupied, Unoccupied, Temporary Occupied.
Cfg Setpoint Type (BV 12) has no access footnote in the table; it is shown as read-only here.
Temperatures are listed in °F; the bulletin also gives the °C range.

source.title: TEC Zoning Control System for Stand-Alone and BACnet MS/TP Networked Applications Technical Bulletin (TEC2647Z-3, TEC2647Z-3+PIR, TEC2664Z-3)

integration.summary: Give each zone controller and rooftop controller a unique MS/TP address, add them to the supervisory controller, then choose the network handle. With Default Zone Handle the supervisor only monitors; with 2 it can schedule each zone through GUI Occupancy (MV 9); with 3 it takes full control.

minimum_points.name: Cfg Network Handle
minimum_points.why: 1 monitor only, 2 zone occupancy, 3 full release

minimum_points.name: GUI PI Heat Weighted Demand
minimum_points.why: Heating demand sent to the rooftop, %

minimum_points.name: GUI PI Cool Weighted Demand
minimum_points.why: Cooling demand sent to the rooftop, %

integration.enable: Cfg Network Handle (MV 7) sets how much control the supervisory controller has: 1 = Default Zone Handle (monitor only, zones follow the rooftop schedule), 2 = Default Minus Occupancy (each zone can be scheduled through GUI Occupancy, MV 9), 3 = Full Release (the supervisor takes full control). The handle can only be written from the supervisory controller, not the zone menu.
integration.remote_sensors: To feed room temperature from the BMS, set GUI Room Temp Override (BV 10) to Override and write GUI Room Temperature (AV 21). GUI Outdoor Temperature (AV 22) is writable.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only; set the MS/TP address (4-127) at the zone controller.
The controller names itself TEC2647Z-72aaa and picks device instance 72aaa (aaa = MS/TP address); change them before mapping points if needed.
Cfg RTC MAC (AV 2) must hold the address of the rooftop controller the zone follows.
gotchas: Zones that do not follow the supervisory schedule usually have the wrong network handle; it is written only from the supervisory controller.
Configuration values (Cfg points) are writable but are setup values; don't write them cyclically.
